analysis: The PR is documentation-only. It changes docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at head line 3, plus a new paragraph in the patch hunk around head lines 252-259) and docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (date bump plus new text at head lines 784-790). The new text says a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates its destinations already available from host bytes. It evaluates or fences none of them, so SSD staging does not wait on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. The import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. This describes a source change in CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift that is not in the supplied evidence, so the code itself was not reviewed. Relevant threats are T-041 (the SSD prefix-cache tier, with its encrypted at-rest posture and the SEC-035 TTFT oracle) and T-029/T-010-style availability concerns. Based only on the doc text, avoiding the evalLock wait could slightly reduce staging latency variance. It could also change the TTFT timing signal for cache hits that T-041 accepts. The DBK3 crypto, HMAC lookup tags, TTL and salt scoping are not described as changed. Host-side plaintext KV bytes are retained as staging scratch, so a deeper review should check that they are zeroed or freed after import, that the scratch charge goes through GlobalKVCacheBudget, and that the import still authenticates (GCM) before creating the destinations. No new findings qualify. Documentation shows no regression, but the underlying Swift change was not supplied, so the next pass should verify it if available. needs_deeper_review is set for that gap rather than as a concrete issue.
